sanskrit: sārasvataṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ babhruvakṣaṃ śītarūre tanvāv asya bhīme | anyedyukaṃ sadandiṃ tvā tṛtīyaka huve namasyaṃ sahadevam apsujam ||
english: The Sārasvata bull, tawny-chested, dreadful in his two forms — O Śītarūra! — the one who strikes every other day, the one who burns perpetually, the tertian: thee I invoke, the one worthy of homage, born together with the gods, born from the waters.

sanskrit: yo apsujo aruṇo mānuṣe jane viveśa babhrur harṣayiṣṇur akṣitaḥ | śītarūrāya tarṣayiṣṇave juguśīrṣasāvayeśaṃ namo astu devāḥ ||
english: He who, born from the waters, ruddy, tawny, indestructible, causing excitement, entered among humankind — to that Śītarūra, the thirst-inducing one, the head-crusher, the overpowering one, may homage be, O gods.

sanskrit: yo harṣayañ jañjabhaḥ svedano vaśī vaśaḥ prāraḥ śītarūrāśiṣe manūn | so asmabhyaṃ mṛḍayan prehi saṃśito yaṃ vayaṃ dviṣmas tam abhi prajānan ||
english: He who, exciting and gnashing, causing perspiration, irresistible by will, by will thrust forth, afflicts mankind for Śītarūra's sake — may he come to us with mercy, sharpened, knowing full well him whom we hate.

sanskrit: namas te vidma te kāsanāyanaṃ yatoyataḥ surabhe saṃbabhūvitha | sa no mā hiṃsīr namo astu tubhyaṃ śīrṣaktyā yakṣmād iha pārayā naḥ ||
english: Homage to thee; we know thy descent from Kāsanā — from whatever place thou wast born, O fragrant one. May he not harm us; homage be to thee. Carry us here safely across the disease of head-ailment and consumption.

sanskrit: asya tvaṃ dadataḥ soma rājan varmeva tanvaṃ pari pāhi viśvataḥ | yo brahmaṇe rādho viddho dadāti tasya soma pra tira dīrgham āyuḥ ||
english: O King Soma, guard the body of this giver from all sides, as if with armour. He who, pierced, gives wealth to a brahmin — for him, O Soma, extend long life.

sanskrit: asya soma pra tira dīrgham āyur ahānīva sūryo vāsarāṇi | māsyā susron nāśayā vyadhmano viṣaṃ bahiḥ śalyaś caratu rogo asmāt ||
english: O Soma, extend his life long, as the sun extends the days one by one. Destroy the poison of well-flowing and ill-blowing months; let the disease go outward, the shaft depart from us.

sanskrit: dānaṃ tṛṣṇāyāḥ pari pātu viddhaṃ dānaṃ kṣudho dānavid eva mṛtyoḥ | aviṣkandho bhavatu yo dadāty ā pyāyate papurir dakṣiṇayā ||
english: Let the gift protect the pierced man against thirst; the gift against hunger — the gift, knowing death. May he who gives be free of viṣkandha disease; the one who has drunk deep is replenished through the sacrificial fee.

sanskrit: ā pyāyatāṃ papurir dakṣiṇayā varmeva syūtaṃ pari pāhi viśvataḥ | bahir viṣaṃ tanvo astv asya sraṃsatāṃ śalyo adhy āre asmāt ||
english: May the one who has drunk deep be replenished through the sacrificial fee; guard him from all sides like stitched armour. Let the poison be outside his body; let the shaft fall away, far from us.

sanskrit: brahmā śaravyām apa bādhatām ito nadyāḥ kūlān nāvam ivādhi śambī | tasmai dadad dīrgham āyuṣ kṛṇuṣva śataṃ ca naḥ śarado jīvatād iha ||
english: Let the brahmin drive the missile-shower away from here, as one steers a boat from the river's bank. Grant long life to him who gives; and may we live here a hundred autumns.

sanskrit: yadā dadāti pradadāti yadā brahmā pratigṛhṇāti rādho asya | ād id vidyād upahatyārātiḥ sarve yakṣmā apa tiṣṭhantu sākam ||
english: When he gives, when he gives abundantly, when the brahmin receives his wealth — then let the foe know he has been struck down; let all diseases stand away together.

sanskrit: vyāghrarūpaḥ surabhiḥ siṃhasya retasā kṛtaḥ | madhye pṛthivyā niṣṭhitaḥ sam akhyad yātudhānyaḥ ||
english: Tiger-formed, fragrant, fashioned from the seed of a lion, established in the middle of the earth — it has beheld the sorceresses utterly.

sanskrit: abhi prehi māpa vikthāḥ pade gṛbhāya māpade | atraiva sarvā jambhaya yāḥ kāś ca yātudhānyaḥ ||
english: Go forward, do not falter; seize at the footprint, do not miss the footprint. Right here devour all of them, whatever sorceresses there may be.

sanskrit: pratībodhaś caturakṣaḥ sraktyo aśmeva vīḍubhit | pratīcīḥ kṛtyā ākṛtya- -amuṃ kṛtyākṛtaṃ jahi ||
english: The counter-waker, four-eyed, angular, shattering like a stone — drawing the counter-sorceries back, slay that sorcery-maker.

sanskrit: kṛtyākṛtaṃ valaginaṃ mūlinaṃ śapatheyyam | indras tu sarvāṃs tān hantu saptaghnena ruvām iva ||
english: The sorcery-maker, the one armed with a staff, the one possessed of root-magic, the one subject to the curse — may Indra slay them all with the seven-slaying weapon, as though howling wolves.
